html:
Black July was the wave of anti Tamil violence in Sri Lanka in July 1983, centred on Colombo. Mobs killed Tamils, burned their homes and shops, and drove tens of thousands from the city. Estimates of the dead run from several hundred to about 3,000.

The trigger was an ambush on 23 July in which the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam killed 13 soldiers in Jaffna. But the attacks were organised: gangs carried voter lists to find Tamil homes, some linked to members of the ruling party, and police often stood by. In Welikada prison, Tamil prisoners were murdered by other inmates.

The roots went back to the Sinhala Only Act of 1956 and decades of discrimination. After Black July, many young Tamils joined the armed groups, and it is taken as the start of the Sri Lankan Civil War, which ran until 2009. It also began a large exodus that built the Tamil diaspora in Canada, Britain and Europe.
